prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: square original source-candidate portrait for future circular game HUD; reviewed at40 and80 pixels.
Task: CP-35.
Primary request: create one head-and-shoulders portrait of William Shakespeare, faithful to the specific original project design in the supplied reference.
Input image1: existing project character front, not a commercial scan or photograph. Effective source status: current canonical front single-card pass8.8; live/raw name Shakespeare; portrait inherits no acceptance. This derivative portrait is proposed source-only; no formal or runtime acceptance transfers.
Subject: William Shakespeare, the same mature author from the supplied project design: high balding forehead, dark-brown wavy hair around the sides and back, fine dark moustache, pointed short goatee, thoughtful warm face, broad ivory pointed Elizabethan collar, ornate black/brown doublet and cape with restrained bronze stitched decoration. Preserve this project face and costume, with no modern actor likeness. No quill, book, hands or text.
Style/medium: refined original collectible-character rendering matching the reference's sculpted forms and hand-painted materials. Simple clear facial landmarks and broad value groups, restrained surface detail. No commercial card-art imitation or requested actor likeness.
Composition: one square image, only head and shoulders, centered face and gaze toward viewer. Keep the complete head, hair, cap or crown including all twig tips inside the full centered circle inscribed in the square. Generous quiet margin above and beside the entire head silhouette; no drawn circle. Shoulders may touch the circle edge. Upper chest low in frame. No full body or pedestal.
Backdrop: quiet uniform dark navy #061623, no scenery.
Lighting: soft studio illumination clearly resolves both eyes and face; no black eye sockets, lens glare, flare or rim glow.
Constraints: no words, letters, numbers, watermark, logo, UI, card frame, border, hands, added props, duplicate face or extra character. No photograph, scan, movie face or actor likeness. Preserve the supplied proposed/canonical design identity and palette without implying new canon, formal acceptance or upstream defect repair.
